subject: Immediate: production throughput drop & GPU pool backpressure — SafeCredit
messages:
From: Emma Liu <emma@safecredit.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Cc: Sales Ops <k_sales@safecredit.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Sudden throughput collapse during morning peak (real-time scoring)

Connor —

We're seeing a dramatic drop in throughput on our production integration starting ~08:45 PT this morning. Errors (502/504) and tail latency have spiked; page load times for transformer scoring pages are >3s and we've had 12 dropped inference batches in the last hour. This is impacting our risk scoring pipeline — we had to route ~15% of traffic to a simple fallback which increases false positives.

I've attached a short set of logs and a summary. Can you confirm this is on Redwood's side and what immediate mitigations you can apply? Our SLA clause for reserved throughput makes this urgent — our Operations and Engineering teams are standing by.

Attachment: svc_logs_20270322.tar.gz (2.1MB)

— Emma
Emma Liu
Head of ML Platform
SafeCredit, Inc.

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@safecredit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse during morning peak (real-time scoring)

Emma — thanks for the quick heads up and for the logs. I’m pulling in our Dedicated support and SREs now.

Immediate notes:
- I’ve escalated to our dedicated GPU pool owners (Vivek + Neha) and asked for a first, protective mitigation: short-term autoscale on additional reserved nodes to catch the tail if capacity sharding fails.
- Can you confirm whether the traffic pattern that started at 08:45 was a spike in concurrency or longer individual sequences? The logs you sent look like chains of long sequences.

I’ll follow up with a status update in 15–20 minutes and will share a timeline for fixes. I know SLAs are tight; we’ll prioritize.

Best,
Connor
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 09:40:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Sudden throughput collapse during morning peak (real-time scoring)

Connor / Team — preliminary triage below (first 20 min):

What we see
- Dedicated pool attached to SafeCredit (pool id: ded-us-west-3-sf-09) shows high head-of-queue backpressure and per-GPU compute saturation starting 08:43 PT.
- Error types are mixed: failed container starts (OOM spike on quantized kernels), and a subsequent increase in request timeouts at the router layer when autoscaler attempted to spin new workers.
- The dominant workload characteristics: long sequence lengths (avg 1.2k tokens) and frequent attention states that prevent KV-cache reuse across requests (low cache hit).

Immediate mitigations applied (09:30–09:38):
- Bumped reserved node pool by +2 nodes (non-blocking warm starts) — reduced queue depth by ~40%.
- Temporarily disabled aggressive packing policy for the pool to reduce OOM churn (packing -> conservative).
- Enabled a fallback model route (lower-memory v2-8q variant) for callers that accept slightly lower quality to preserve latency for critical traffic.

Next steps (ETA):
- 2 hours: apply tuned kernel schedule for long sequence paths (Neha).
- 4 hours: roll a per-customer KV-cache affinity to improve reuse (engineering change + config).
- Exec note: if we can't restore promised reserved throughput within 12 hours, we should prepare credits/contract remedies.

I’ll attach a short perf dump and QoS summary once post-mitigation data comes in.

— Vivek
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference
Attachment: qos_summary_safecredit_Mar22.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Emma Liu <emma@safecredit.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek_kulkarni@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 22 Mar 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Sudden throughput collapse during morning peak (real-time scoring)

Emma — quick update from the team:

- We observed compute saturation due to a sudden pattern of longer sequences, which interacted poorly with our existing packing/quantization profile for your pool.
- We’ve added two reserved nodes and temporarily routed 30% of high-length requests to a lower-memory variant (quality tradeoff). This reduced observed 95th percentile latency from ~2.8s to ~850ms in the last 20 minutes.
- We will be deploying a kernel scheduling tweak and a per-customer cache affinity change; target for full stabilization is today EOD PT.

We know this is impacting your operations — if you'd like an exec-to-exec sync, Marissa (cc) can join. We will also provide a short postmortem and the QoS summary.

Connor
Customer Success — Redwood Inference

Team — forwarding the thread. TL;DR: SafeCredit is a mid-enterprise reserved customer on an annual committed plan (RW-2026-SAFE-12). They experienced a reserved throughput shortfall during their morning peak due to pool saturation + packing mismatch. Engineering applied mitigations that reduced latency significantly but did not fully restore the committed throughput for ~2 hours.

Asks:
- Finance: please prepare a credit estimate (prorated portion for 2 hours of shortfall + customer goodwill credit).
- Legal/Contracts: review whether we owe formal SLA remediation under section 4.2 (reserved throughput).
- Leadership: recommend an exec sync with SafeCredit within 4 hours to avoid escalation; I'll join.

I’ll schedule a 1:1 with Emma if they accept; Connor, please attach the QoS post-mitigation report in the shared Drive link (HS-12457).

— Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference

Date: Wed, 24 Mar 2027 18:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Immediate: production throughput drop & GPU pool backpressure — SafeCredit

Emma — quick follow-up with final actions & commitments:

What happened (summary):
- At ~08:43 PT on 2027-03-22, customer workload pattern shifted to longer sequences and lower KV-cache reuse, which caused per-GPU compute saturation and OOMs during container starts. The autoscaler response created transient router timeouts.

Actions completed:
- +2 reserved nodes added (immediate) and packing policy tuned to conservative for your pool.
- Kernel scheduling tweak deployed 2027-03-22 14:10 PT (reduced long-seq kernel stalls).
- Per-customer KV-cache affinity rollout started and completed 2027-03-24 15:30 PT for SafeCredit.
- QoS/metrics: 95th latency is back to target for last 24h; error rate dropped to baseline. Post-incident report: https://drive.redwood/safecredit/incident-20270322 (HS-12457)

Compensation & next steps:
- Finance/legal are preparing a prorated credit for the impacted window; Marissa is coordinating and will share the figure.
- We propose a joint technical review next week to discuss: model variants, packing profiles, and defensive autoscale thresholds.

We appreciate your patience — sorry for the disruption. If you want an immediate exec-to-exec call, Marissa and I are available this afternoon.

Best,
Connor O'Brien
Customer Success — Redwood Inference
